item.title: Automated end-station at the soft X-ray beamline featuring robotic air-to-ultrahigh-vacuum sample transfer, scanning probe spectroscopy, and machine learning analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.22384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driven by the growing integration of artificial intelligence and robotics in experimental science, we redefine the execution of user experiments at synchrotron soft X-ray beamlines by developing a highly automated end-station that can be operated without on-site staff. Installed at beamline BL08U of NanoTerasu, the system comprises four chamber units and two robots that automatically transfer samples from ambient air to an ultrahigh vacuum measurement stage for spectroscopic evaluations, before returning them to their original locations post-measurement. Soft X-ray absorption spectra are automatically acquired once programmed by scanning the micro-focused beam over the designated sample area, followed by automated evaluation using machine learning techniques such as principal-component analysis, multidimensional scaling, t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, and uniform manifold approximation and projection. The high-throughput data are systematically accumulated in the database for remote user examination. This unstaffed end-station provides efficient beamtime for users and allows beamline scientists/technicians to pursue more human and creative endeavors.
item.dc:creator: Keita Hiromori, Masashige Miyamoto, Masafumi Horio, Takeru Nakashima, Yasunobu Ando, Masato Kotsugi, Iwao Matsuda

item.title: Long-Lived Charge Trap Characterization for Rare-Event Searches with Skipper-CCDs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skipper Charge-Coupled Devices (Skipper-CCDs) are detectors with sub-electron resolution, allowing them to play a critical role in rare-event searches. A major challenge in experiments using these detectors is understanding and mitigating low-energy backgrounds which impact the single-electron rate. One potential component of the single-electron rate could arise from single-electron charge traps caused by lattice defects. In this work we use a new in-situ technique for generating uniform charge known as ``pixel-pumping'' across the CCD to study single-electron traps in a SENSEI sensor placed underground in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab, which enables sensitivity to long-lived traps with emission times $>10^3$ seconds, a regime that was previously not accessible. We fully characterize 1787 traps and use this information to estimate their contribution to the single-electron background in SENSEI. Through simulation, we find the characterized population of traps does not significantly impact the single-electron rate. We further identify the energies and cross-sections for traps to which this analysis is sensitive, and compare this with the values that could impact the single-electron rate. This analysis probes a large fraction of this region. However, we also see that a sufficiently numerous hidden population could contribute significantly to the single-electron rate, and new measurement techniques will have to be devised in order to fully rule out this population.

item.title: Improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response in athermal phonon detectors: implications for quasiparticle dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our detectors for Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino--Nucleus Scattering (CE$\nu$NS) use photolithographically patterned superconducting athermal phonon sensors that are coupled to kg-scale absorbers of different materials (germanium, silicon, sapphire). Following a particle interaction, athermal phonons from the bulk absorber break Cooper pairs in a superconducting aluminum film that surrounds a tungsten Transition Edge Sensor (TES) in equilibrium through electrothermal feedback. This sensor design is called Quasiparticle-trap-assisted Electro-thermal-feedback Transition-edge-sensor (QET). The QET aluminum film that absorbs the athermal phonons is patterned into fins with lengths limited by the quasiparticle diffusion length in aluminum. Improving the quasiparticle diffusion length in the superconducting aluminum is an area of vigorous research to improve phonon collection efficiency and increase the signal strength for lower-threshold searches. We report significantly improved aluminum films that show systematically larger grain sizes and residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) compared to detectors we have fabricated in the past. The improved RRR and grain sizes were expected to improve the collected signal for a given energy. We report higher signal strength achieved in a detector in comparison to another detector in which all other fabrication parameters were kept identical except for the aluminum film deposition.
item.dc:creator: Mahdi Mirzakhani, Keith Hunter, Rupak Mahapatra, Mark Platt

item.title: A dry cryogenic platform with picometre stability for nanoscale and quantum technologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.23407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanically ultrastable environments within maintenance-free dry cryostats are needed for high-precision surface probe microscopy experiments, as well as next-generation quantum technologies. The most demanding applications require picometre-scale precision combined with multi-axis and millimetre-scale scanning range, while offering access to optical, microwave, and radiofrequency control and a vector magnetic field. We demonstrate a versatile platform for such systems based on passive and active vibration control for a commercial dry cryostat. Using a tunable optical microcavity as a sensor, we report vibration levels of 4.2 pm root mean square at 2.3 K over one hour without postselection. We further demonstrate drift-free long-term operation with stability below 8.6 pm RMS over 12 hours. Our system enables continuous and automated operation for next-generation high-throughput applications without the need for liquid helium infrastructure. Requiring only standard machining facilities and commercially available hardware, the design can be readily adapted for cryogenic optical, electrical and magnetic high-precision measurements across quantum science, surface science, and nanotechnology.
item.dc:creator: William G. Roth, Andreas Thurn, Alexander M. Stramma, Amit R. Dhawan, Jason M. Smith, Dorian A. Gangloff, Mete Atat\"ure

item.title: Reconstruction of Magnetic Fields with a Physics-Informed Neural Network
item.description: arXiv:2610.23691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate reconstruction of magnetic fields and their gradients is essential for assessing and controlling systematic effects in precision measurement experiments. We have developed a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method which reconstructs three-dimensional magnetic fields subject to the source-free Maxwell equations, $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}=0$ and $\nabla\times\mathbf{B}=\mathbf{0}$. In an extension of our previous work on PINN methods for reconstruction of magnetic fields in inaccessible interior regions via measurements at exterior locations, we now demonstrate the feasibility of applying PINN methods to the extraction of magnetic field gradient terms from discrete measurement points subject to constraints from Maxwell's equations.

item.title: Results from the GIF++ Long-Term Study of Eco-Friendly Gas Mixtures for RPCs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaseous detectors play a crucial role in high-energy physics experiments, yet their operation often relies on fluorinated gases with a very high Global Warming Potential (GWP). Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) operated in avalanche mode typically use high-performance gas mixtures based on high-GWP F-gases such as C$_2$H$_2$F$_4$ and SF$_6$. As environmental concerns grow and regulations become increasingly stringent, the development of sustainable gas mixtures has become a global priority. Within the RPC ECOGas@GIF++ Collaboration, a long-term R&D program has investigated eco-friendly gas mixtures for RPCs and assessed their performance under irradiation. RPCs operated with an HFO-1234ze/CO$_2$ mixture were exposed to high particle fluxes at CERN GIF++, accumulating $\mathcal{O}(10^2~\mathrm{mC/cm^2})$ over three years. This ageing campaign is now complete, and the detector performances have been systematically evaluated across a broad range of particle rates. This paper presents preliminary final results from the campaign, along with future perspectives.

item.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
item.description: arXiv:2610.23810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at $f_s$ is indistinguishable from one at $f_p - f_s$, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180$^{\circ}$ hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Klimovich, Peter K. Day, Henry G. Leduc, Boon-Kok Tan

item.title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) offers a unique opportunity to map the QCD phase diagram in the high-baryon-density region. In particular, higher-order cumulants ($C_r$) of event-by-event proton number distributions have been proposed as sensitive probes of the nuclear-matter phase structure. In this work, $^{\text{238}}$U+$^{\text{238}}$U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV are generated using the JAM2 model and then processed through the CEE fast simulation with detector responses. Experimental analysis procedures, including centrality determination and particle identification, are also implemented. Proton-number cumulants up to fourth order and their ratios are calculated and compared with the true values. A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. An additional factor is also included to account for acceptance losses caused by the azimuthal gap between the two TPCs. Within the uncertainties of the current data sample, the corrected cumulants and cumulant ratios are consistent with their generator-level values. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. These results provide a simulation-based assessment of the analysis feasibility and statistical requirements for proton-number fluctuation measurements at CEE.
item.dc:creator: Shuaike Lv, Fan Si, Xionghong He, Xu Sun, Yige Huang, Wanbing He, Yifei Zhang, Ming Shao, Ziyang Li

item.title: Towards Low-Energy Electron High-Resolution Spectroscopy with Transition-Edge Sensors
item.description: arXiv:2602.21694v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a study of the energy resolution of transition-edge sensors (TESs) for the detection of electrons in the 100~eV kinetic energy range. The TES is a Ti-Au bilayer with an active area of ($60 \times 60$) $\mu$m$^2$ and a critical temperature of $\sim 80$~mK. The electron source is based on vertically-aligned multiwall carbon nanotubes located inside the cryostat, with electrons generated via field emission. For electrons in the $(92 - 99)$~eV kinetic energy range, we obtain a Gaussian energy resolution for fully-absorbed electrons of ($0.48 \pm 0.04 \pm 0.06$)~eV, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic}. When considering the full-width at half-maximum of the peak \textcolor{black}{of the signal amplitude distribution}, the corresponding resolution is of ($1.4 \pm 0.2 \pm 0.3$)~eV. The former represents an improvement of $(47-60)\%$ with respect to previous results, and is mainly attributed to the reduction in the TES active area. The latter is instead an improvement of over a factor of 21, and is mainly due to the reduction in the emitting area of the electron source, which significantly suppresses electron back-scattering in proximity of the TES. These results represent a major milestone towards high-precision spectroscopy on low-energy electrons, which is a key objective for the PTOLEMY experiment.

item.title: Machine Learning on Heterogeneous, Edge, and Quantum Hardware for Particle Physics (ML-HEQUPP)
item.description: arXiv:2602.22248v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The next generation of particle physics experiments will face a new era of challenges in data acquisition, due to unprecedented data rates and volumes along with extreme environments and operational constraints. Harnessing this data for scientific discovery demands real-time inference and decision-making, intelligent data reduction, and efficient processing architectures beyond current capabilities. Crucial to the success of this experimental paradigm are several emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), silicon microelectronics, and the advent of quantum algorithms and processing. Their intersection includes areas of research such as low-power and low-latency devices for edge computing, heterogeneous accelerator systems, reconfigurable hardware, novel codesign and synthesis strategies, readout for cryogenic or high-radiation environments, and analog computing. This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, contributing towards a successful transition to the new data frontier of fundamental science.

item.title: Suppression of $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ photon hits in large liquid scintillator detectors via spatiotemporal deep learning
item.description: arXiv:2603.27727v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Liquid scintillator detectors are widely used in neutrino experiments due to their low energy threshold and high energy resolution. Despite the tiny abundance of $^{14}$C in LS, the photons induced by the $\beta$ decay of the $^{14}$C isotope inevitably contaminate the signal, degrading the energy resolution. In this work, we propose three models to tag $^{14}$C photon hits in e$^+$ events with $^{14}$C pile-up, thereby suppressing its impact on the energy resolution at the hit level: a gated spatiotemporal graph neural network and two Transformer-based models with scalar and vector charge encoding. For a simulated test dataset in which each event contains one $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ and one e$^+$ with kinetic energy below 5 MeV, the models achieve $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ recall rates of 25%-48% while maintaining $\mathrm{e}^{+}$ to $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ misidentification below 1%, leading to a large improvement in the resolution of total charge for events where $\mathrm{e}^{+}$ and $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ photon hits strongly overlap in space and time.
item.dc:creator: Junle Li, Zhaoxiang Wu, Guanda Gong, Zhaohan Li, Wuming Luo, Jiahui Wei, Wenxing Fang, Hehe Fan

item.title: Deep-learning-based low-energy trigger algorithms for the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment
item.description: arXiv:2605.31391v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern machine learning techniques have become increasingly important in particle physics because of their powerful pattern-recognition capabilities, including in real-time data acquisition where stringent runtime constraints apply. This paper details the performance of deep-learning-based trigger algorithms for a large water Cherenkov detector such as Hyper-Kamiokande, aimed at low-energy neutrino events (below 7 MeV). The performance of custom neural-network supervised classifiers is shown alongside two anomaly-detection approaches trained solely on detector noise: a pure autoencoder and a model based on Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery. The supervised model shows signal identification efficiencies of 76.7% for single electrons of 3 MeV kinetic energy, significantly exceeding signal efficiencies obtained from a traditional hit-count-based trigger of 26.4%, while the Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery approach reaches 35.4% at the same operating point. Runtime evaluations on GPU yield per-window inference latencies well below the millisecond scale.
item.dc:creator: Katharina Lachner, Sa\'ul Alonso-Monsalve, Benjamin Richards, Davide Sgalaberna

item.title: First evaluation of the tracking performance of the ARCADIA Fully Depleted MAPS with high-energy proton beam
item.description: arXiv:2606.25655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents test beam characterization of the ARCADIA Main Demonstrator 3, a 200 $\mu$m thick Fully Depleted MAPS developed using a custom LFoundry 110 nm CIS process on a high-resistivity substrate. Measurements using a 120 GeV proton beam demonstrate a detection efficiency exceeding 99% and a spatial resolution down to 3.8 $\mu$m. The study evaluates cluster size, spatial resolution, and efficiency as a function of the threshold and reverse bias voltage.

item.title: A New High-Intensity Source for Ultracold Neutrons
item.description: arXiv:2607.03033v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The TRIUMF UltraCold Advanced Neutron (TUCAN) collaboration has completed a new superthermal source for ultracold neutrons (UCNs) at TRIUMF. Neutrons produced in a spallation target are moderated in heavy water and liquid deuterium, and are converted to ultracold neutrons by inelastic scattering inside superfluid $^4$He at around 1.1 K. During commissioning of the completed moderation and conversion system, including the liquid-deuterium moderator, up to $1.47(2)\times 10^7$ UCNs were detected outside the source in the experimental area following a 60 s accumulation period. At the same location, continuous operation produced detector rates of up to $6.75(3)\times 10^7$ UCN/s, and a density of 165.6(1) UCN/cm$^3$ was achieved in a 25.4 L external vessel. These measurements demonstrate high-intensity operation of a spallation-driven He-II UCN source, including extraction and transport to an external experimental area.

item.title: Optical Characterization Measurements of Commercial Polyvinyltoluene Scintillators for Accurate Geant4 Detector Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2608.13710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate Monte Carlo simulation of plastic scintillator detectors requires precise wavelength-dependent optical properties. We present measurements of wavelength-dependent refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and bulk absorption length $L_{\mathrm{abs}}(\lambda)$ for six commercial polyvinyltoluene (PVT)-based scintillators (Saint Gobain BC-400, BC-404, BC-408, BC-418, BC-422, and BC-430) at five wavelengths between 372 and 660 nm. Using a precision refraction apparatus and variable-thickness transmission measurements, we characterize material-specific dispersion that deviates substantially from both the manufacturer specification and literature values for pure PVT. Illustrative Geant4 simulations of a BC-422 detector demonstrate a 7.2% reduction in photocathode energy-deposition threshold events when using our measured $n(\lambda)$ compared to the constant manufacturer value, highlighting the practical importance of accurate optical property data for detector design and calibration. We successfully measure absorption lengths for BC-430 at four wavelengths between 372 and 505 nm (2.2-12.4 mm) and for all materials at 372 nm (2.2-38 mm), while establishing lower bounds exceeding 750 mm for weakly absorbing formulations at longer wavelengths.
item.dc:creator: Fergus Martin Huggins, Micah S. Johnson, Matthew Quinn Buckner

item.title: In Situ Three-Dimensional Mapping of Lithiation Heterogeneity in NMC Electrodes using XANES Nanotomography
item.description: arXiv:2307.08871v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in lithiation complicates the interpretation of electrode-averaged electrochemical measurements and the assessment of local active-material utilization. Here, we use three-energy X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) nanotomography to investigate lithiation distributions in NMC532 composite electrodes with active-material loadings of 3 and 15 mg cm-2. Tomographic acquisitions at 8.30, 8.35, and 8.43 keV combine three-dimensional particle morphology with Ni K-edge chemical sensitivity at a processed voxel size of 210 nm. The normalized absorption contrast serves as a relative lithiation indicator, without assigning absolute lithium concentrations. Measurements were performed in situ after 1 h of open-circuit relaxation at selected electrochemical states. In the lower-loading electrode, four successive states during interrupted discharge at 2 mA cm-2 reveal an increasing lithium-rich volume fraction alongside core-shell-like distributions, nonuniform peripheral enrichment, and particle-to-particle variability. In the higher-loading electrode, two regions examined at 50% depth of discharge exhibit different lithiation-sensitive contrast distributions despite sharing the same nominal electrochemical state. These observations document heterogeneity within particles, between particles, and between electrode regions, showing how overall lithiation progression can coexist with spatially nonuniform local states. Three-energy XANES nanotomography thus provides a means of examining lithiation heterogeneity in dense composite electrodes with limited spectral sampling. Correlative phase-contrast imaging could further relate these distributions to the arrangement of the carbon-binder domain and pore network.
item.dc:creator: Tuan-Tu Nguyen, Jiahui Xu, Zeliang Su, Vincent De Andrade, Alejandro A. Franco, Bruno Delobel, Charles Delacourt, Arnaud Demorti\`ere

item.title: Nested active pointing control for interspacecraft laser interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2606.21274v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Precise pointing control is critical for interspacecraft laser interferometry, as angular misalignment introduces measurement noise and can even lead to laser link loss. We present a nested control architecture that uses differential wavefront sensing signals to drive a fast steering mirror (FSM) to track the incoming beam, while feeding the FSM deflections back to the attitude and orbit control system to suppress angle-dependent optical path variations. This scheme is experimentally validated in our hexapod-based setup. Relative to standalone FSM actuation, the nested configuration reduced the low-frequency root-mean-square pointing jitter by approximately a factor of 2 over 3--70 mHz in both directions. Additionally, tilt-to-length coupling was suppressed by an order of magnitude below 5 mHz and by two orders of magnitude below 0.5 mHz. These results demonstrate the feasibility of nested active pointing control for future interspacecraft laser interferometry missions.
item.dc:creator: Daikang Wei, Christoph Bode, Yihao Yan, Vitali M\"uller, Juan Jos\'e Esteban Delgado, Gerhard Heinzel

item.title: Residual diagnostics for detecting the breakdown of the single power-law approximation in photoelectron yield spectroscopy: application to doped silicon
item.description: arXiv:2610.11331v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Our automated analysis of photoelectron yield spectroscopy (PYS) estimates the threshold Ith and the exponent n of a single power law for every spectrum. When this model fits poorly, however, the analysis cannot tell whether the data or the model is at fault. Here we present residual diagnostics that separate the two causes. The exponent is scanned continuously on a 1/n-power fit with an Akaike information criterion (AIC) based on the mean absolute error (MAE), and the spread of the resulting Akaike weights ($P \times \Delta n$) quantifies the uncertainty of the estimate. The normalized MAE (NMAE) and the RMSE-to-MAE ratio (RMR) assess the data quality, the Durbin-Watson (DW) statistic assesses the model adequacy, and the three checks are reported in parallel. With criteria set from an Au reference, the diagnostics were applied to 60 continuous measurements in air of four HF-treated Si samples. For heavily doped p-type Si, DW fell below its criterion, whereas the means of NMAE and RMR remained within their criteria. Prompted by this flag, we fitted the spectrum with a two-component model with fixed exponents (n = 1 and 2.5); the AIC decreased by 56, DW increased from 0.86 to 1.99, and the two components set in at 4.70 and 5.28 eV. For heavily doped n-type Si, the change during air exposure was consistent with a single component. The diagnostics thus identify the spectra that require a multi-component analysis without assuming an emission mechanism.
